newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes-Benz to reshape logistics strategy.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes-Benz to reshape logistics strategy.

text.p: Mercedes-Benz AG said it will launch a re-structured global logistics strategy for its automobile parts distribution in 1997.

Rolf Hoeschele, logistics planning manager for the company's automobile parts centre, said the new strategy would speed up spare parts distribution and integrate manufacturing plants in the U.S., South America and Asia.

In a three-year first stage starting next year, wholesalers in western Europe will be covered from nine warehouses instead of 21 national parts centres, he said in a presentation to the German Logistics Congress in Berlin, which ended on Friday.
A concept for eastern Europe, Greece and Turkey is being developed and the new logistics strategy will be fully internationalised later on the basis of experience in Europe, Hoeschele said.
Items will be transported to warehouses by forwarders or express services as an overnight service or as a day-time service from hubs, he added.
"We are seeking close logistics partnerships with our parts suppliers. This put them in a position to manage their production and deliver just in time," Hoeschele said.
A new communications system will link retailers, the company parts division and forwarders, express services and logistics services providers.
Mercedes-Benz would maintain its round-the-clock emergency service to ensure rapid delivery in urgent cases, he added.
"The emergency service ensures supply of parts and uses all available structures -- express services, airlines, helicopters, and so on," Hoeschele added.
The Mercedes-Benz parts centre, with 3,500 employees, is part of the company's sales division and includes marketing, logistics planning, warehousing and operations.
The company currently holds 280,000 items in storage and purchases another 100,00 items according to client needs.

By 2000, the company plans to hold 470,000 items in storage plus purchase items according to client demand, and provide a higher level of parts availability at points of sale, Hoeschele said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
